home.hero.title:
Hi! I’m Anastasia,
a product designer.
home.hero.subtitle: For more than 5 years I’ve been designing usable, intuitive interfaces that connect business goals with user needs.
home.experience.title: Work experience
home.experience.intro: In recent years I’ve worked on fintech mobile apps and high-load B2B systems. I’ve joined projects at different stages — from building products from scratch at startups to scaling and improving features at large companies.
home.exp.kr.desc: I worked on digital products for large Russian clients in the public sector and utilities. I designed complex internal B2B systems, customer portals, and services with AI assistants.
home.exp.minvest.desc: I took part in launching the first investment platform in Kyrgyzstan. On this project I designed the mobile app, website, and an internal CRM for the team.
home.exp.ipc.desc: I designed the Elkart Mobile app for money transfers and payments in Kyrgyzstan. I contributed to the platform’s digital transformation with a redesign that improved the user experience.
home.exp.jetstyle.desc: I designed for commerce, healthcare, and delivery products — mobile apps, multi-page websites, and online stores.
home.exp.self.desc: I developed design concepts for a range of projects, including creating and preparing layouts.
home.skills.title: Focus areas
home.skills.product.title: Product design
home.skills.product.desc: I think about the product as a whole — from early research and prototyping to launch and optimization. Design should help users reach their goals quickly and also improve key product metrics.
home.skills.ux.title: UX research
home.skills.ux.desc: I research users, analyze behavior, and test hypotheses to make informed design decisions. Methods include in-depth interviews, usability and A/B tests, CJM, personas, and more.
home.skills.ds.title: Design systems
home.skills.ds.desc: I build a shared visual language, scalable UI components, and documentation so teams can move faster while keeping interfaces consistent.
home.skills.collab.title: Collaboration with engineers, PMs, and analysts
home.skills.collab.desc: I work closely with everyone involved in building the product, balancing technical constraints, user expectations, and business goals. I aim for transparent processes and effective collaboration.
about.hero.name: Anastasia Kobeleva
about.hero.bio: I’ve been in design for more than 5 years, including 2 years in fintech. My approach is grounded in research into users, business goals, and technical constraints. Great product design is not only polished UI — it is a well-thought-out interaction model that makes the product simple and intuitive.
about.experience.title: Work experience
about.exp.kr.about: KR Digital is a digital studio that builds innovative solutions.
about.exp.kr.tasksHtml: Key responsibilities: Design and evolve complex digital products for large corporate and public-sector clients. Map user flows, business logic, and new features with many states and constraints.
about.exp.kr.solutionHtml:
Solution:
— Moscow Department of IT: designed new features for internal task-management (Jira-like) and knowledge (Confluence-like) systems. One of the largest modules was a workflow editor with validators and post-functions; I defined the structure, states, dependencies, and configuration logic for complex business rules.
— Mosoblgaz: evolved the mobile and web customer portal; contributed to launching a chat with an AI assistant.
— Migrant app: designed flows for patent-status tracking, document upload, and multi-step processes.
about.exp.kr.resultHtml:
Outcome:
— Turned complex workflow configuration — validators, post-functions, dependencies, and business constraints — into a coherent management interface.
— Designed and evolved user flows for products with different audiences and domains, from internal corporate systems to mass-market mobile apps.
about.exp.minvest.about: MINVEST is the first digital brokerage platform in Kyrgyzstan.
about.exp.minvest.tasksHtml: Key responsibilities: Launch an investment platform with an intuitive interface. Attract X k active users by year-end. Design the website and an internal CRM so staff can work quickly and comfortably.
about.exp.minvest.solutionHtml:
Solution:
— Designed core app functionality.
— Evolved the internal CRM based on team feedback.
— Ran UX research (interviews, usability tests, A/B tests) to improve ease of use.
— Designed and improved the website, education platform, and overall brand design strategy.
about.exp.minvest.resultHtml:
Outcome:
— Successful launch with full trading and analytics functionality.
— Strong activation conversion thanks to an intuitive interface and a simplified sign-up flow.
— Higher engagement through improved UX.
— X k active users by the end of 2024.
— Stronger brand through a connected digital ecosystem.
about.exp.ipc.about: Elkart Mobile is a finance app for transfers and payments in Kyrgyzstan, with an active audience of more than 300k users.
about.exp.ipc.tasksHtml: Key responsibilities: Improve usability and functionality through a redesign and new services.
about.exp.ipc.solutionHtml:
Solution:
— Delivered a full redesign that improved usability and visual appeal.
— Designed new services.
— Ran user research and usability testing to find friction and improve how people use banking services.
about.exp.ipc.resultHtml:
Outcome:
— Improved app usability, which increased satisfaction and engagement.
— New service sections and government services expanded the product and grew active users.
— The redesign also helped optimize app performance.
about.exp.jetstyle.about: JetStyle is a digital agency focused on UX/UI design, web development, and digital marketing. I designed interfaces for e-commerce, healthcare, and delivery (mobile apps, websites, and online stores).
about.exp.jetstyle.tasksHtml:
Key responsibilities and results:
‍— Redesigned platforms, which increased conversion and engagement.
— Ran UX audits and user research to find problem areas and improve usability.
— Presented and defended design decisions to stakeholders and product managers.
— Built UI kits, components, and interface elements.
about.exp.self.about: I developed design concepts for various projects, including creating and preparing layouts and adapting them across platforms.
about.exp.self.bulletsHtml:
— Ran competitor analysis, market research, and user interviews.
— Built CJMs, personas, and empathy maps to understand and meet user needs.
— Prepared presentations and justified design decisions for clients.

about.education.school: Ural State University of Architecture and Art
about.skills.title: Skills
about.skills.ui.title: UI design
about.skills.ui.desc: I have a solid grasp of visual design — color, composition, and typography. I aim for interfaces that look considered and speak to the target audience. I keep learning and looking for ways to level up.
about.skills.ux.title: UX research
about.skills.ux.desc: I apply UX principles to create intuitive, comfortable interfaces. Research, prototyping, and usability testing help me find the right solutions and make the product genuinely easy to use.
about.skills.graphic.title: Graphic design and illustration
about.skills.graphic.desc: With an art background, I create 2D and 3D illustrations, icons, and other graphics. That lets me bring visual elements into interfaces and increase user response.
about.skills.tools.title: Tools
about.skills.tools.desc: Figma, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe After Effects, Spline, Webflow, Basic HTML & CSS.
about.skills.langs.title: Languages
about.bio.p1: I try to look at the product through the user’s eyes — what will feel easy, where friction might appear, and how to make the experience pleasant. I like digging into details, understanding how the product works, researching, and finding solutions that actually help people.
about.bio.p2: Working as a team matters to me — discussing ideas, asking questions, and finding better solutions together. I believe good communication and collaboration make the product stronger.
about.bio.p3: Beyond design I care about art and music, and I keep learning. In my free time I draw, explore 3D, and try new tools for visualizing ideas.
about.inspire.title: What inspires me?
about.inspire.desc: I have a degree in fine arts, so I especially value the balance between function and aesthetics. Art and music give me fresh ideas and help me make digital work more expressive. I like that product design mixes creativity, analysis, and an understanding of user behavior — that makes every brief genuinely interesting.
fintrack.hero.title: Fintrack — finance and goals tracker
fintrack.about.title: About the project
fintrack.about.p1Html: Fintrack is a personal-finance app that helps people control their budget, analyze spending, and reach financial goals.
fintrack.about.p2Html: Target market: global, with a focus on people who want to build financial literacy.
fintrack.goals.task: Design a clear, intuitive app for tracking finances. The experience should feel simple, understandable, and motivating so people can manage money with confidence and reach their goals.
fintrack.goals.solutionIntro: I designed a concept that covers the full money-management journey:
fintrack.goals.solution2: ✦ Spending visualization that makes the current picture easy to grasp.
fintrack.goals.solution3: ✦ Charts for account status and category spending stats.
fintrack.goals.solution4: ✦ Goals for savings and major purchases, with progress over time.
fintrack.goals.solution5: ✦ An emotional yet clean UI that does not distract from the main task.
fintrack.goals.result: A product that makes financial control accessible and convenient.
fintrack.goals.scaleHtml: Scale potential: the interface is ready to adapt to different markets and audiences.
fintrack.process.title: Design process
fintrack.process.1: 1. Domain research: analysis of other finance-tracking apps.
fintrack.research.title: Research
fintrack.research.intro: To define the audience and check whether this kind of product is relevant, I ran several interviews. I wanted to learn how people track money, which budget tools they use — if any — and how they save toward dreams and goals: keeping numbers in their head or using visualization tools. That helped me understand needs more deeply and fold them into the project.
fintrack.research.questionsIntro: The main questions I needed to answer:
fintrack.research.q1: ❓ Do you track your monthly expenses and income?
fintrack.research.q2: ❓ If yes, which tools do you use?
fintrack.research.q4: ❓ What difficulties do you face when using apps and analyzing your finances?
fintrack.research.q5: ❓What would an ideal finance app look like for you?
fintrack.research.q6: ❓ Which tools and features matter most to you, and why?
fintrack.research.q7: ❓ Do you use any tool to visualize your goals?
fintrack.insights.title: Insights
fintrack.insights.intro: After the interviews I grouped a few key insights:
fintrack.insights.1.title: People use a mix of tools and are not always happy with them.
fintrack.insights.1.titleMobileHtml: 1     People use a mix of tools and are not always happy with them.
fintrack.insights.1.desc: People often keep accounts at different banks — a salary card in one, a credit card in another, a savings account in a third. That makes a single picture hard to keep, which often leads to extra spending.
fintrack.insights.2.title: Many people save toward big goals but have no clear system.
fintrack.insights.2.titleMobileHtml: 2     Many people save toward big goals but have no clear system.
fintrack.insights.2.desc: Some keep the target in their head, others move money to a separate account, but there is no convenient visual tool that shows progress.
fintrack.insights.3.title: Most people want to control their finances but do not do it consistently.
fintrack.insights.3.titleMobileHtml: 3     Most people want to control their finances but do not do it consistently.
fintrack.insights.3.desc: Many said they started tracking and then dropped it because it took too much time or felt inconvenient.
fintrack.problem.title: Problem
fintrack.problem.intro: I combined the findings into one core problem:
fintrack.problem.statement: People struggle to track income and expenses because most existing products are overloaded, inconvenient, or fail to show a full financial picture. Split accounts across apps and cash spending that is hard to log by hand make it worse.
fintrack.hypotheses.title: Hypotheses
fintrack.hypotheses.intro: Next I formed hypotheses about what would make the app more useful. I then tested them and thought through how they would fit the interface and help users.
fintrack.hypotheses.1.title: Stats and analytics
fintrack.hypotheses.1.desc: If income and expenses are shown as charts, people will understand where their money goes faster.
fintrack.hypotheses.2.title: Intuitiveness
fintrack.hypotheses.2.desc: If the interface is simple and clear, people will figure it out quickly and start using the app.
fintrack.hypotheses.3.title: Financial goals
fintrack.hypotheses.3.desc: Financial goals will add a new layer of value and attract more users.
fintrack.hypotheses.4.title: Spending categories
fintrack.hypotheses.4.desc: If people can edit categories and create their own, everyone can fit the app to their money habits.
fintrack.hypotheses.5.title: Motivation
fintrack.hypotheses.5.desc: Visualizing financial goals can motivate people to save more deliberately.
fintrack.hypotheses.6.title: Optional sign-in
fintrack.hypotheses.6.desc: If sign-in is optional, people can reach core features immediately. That lowers the barrier to start.
fintrack.competitors.title: Competitive analysis
fintrack.competitors.desc: I also reviewed other finance apps: which features they offer, what feels convenient, and what may cause friction. That showed what to keep and what to improve so the product is useful and easy to use.
fintrack.persona.title: User persona
fintrack.persona.name: Alexey, 30
fintrack.persona.motivationHtml:
— Wants to manage money well in order to reach his goals.
— Aims for financial stability and independence.
fintrack.persona.goalsHtml:
— Saving toward a family vacation this summer.
— Putting part of his salary toward buying a home.
— Wants to avoid financial chaos and see a real picture of income and expenses.
fintrack.persona.painHtml:
— Income and expenses are split across accounts and cash.
— No convenient tool for tracking savings toward big goals.
— No motivation or reminders around financial goals.
fintrack.empathy.title: Empathy map
fintrack.solution.title: Solution
fintrack.solution.home.title: Home screen with budget
fintrack.solution.home.descHtml:
The home screen shows financial status: balance, spend this month, recent transactions, and popular categories. Key information is in one place so people can assess the situation without extra taps.
✔ Core metrics are large and easy to scan.
✔ A new transaction can be added quickly.
✔ No clutter — only what matters.
fintrack.solution.add.title: Adding a transaction
fintrack.solution.add.p1Html: Users can add a transaction quickly by entering an amount and choosing a category, account, and date. A comment is optional.
fintrack.solution.add.p2: I kept adding a transaction as simple as possible — chips for frequent amounts, easy account and date pickers, and clear icon categories. The whole action takes a few seconds.
fintrack.solution.history.title: History
fintrack.solution.history.desc: This section lists all transactions — spending and income. I focused on making the list readable and structured: filters for fast search, a visual split between outflows and inflows, and totals for expenses and income.
fintrack.solution.details.title: Transaction details
fintrack.solution.details.desc: Opens from a history item. It shows the full transaction (amount, date, account, category, comment). Users can edit or delete it.
fintrack.solution.analytics.title: Analytics
fintrack.solution.analytics.p1Html: Analytics is one of the core features. Users can track income and expense trends, spot patterns, and see where money goes.
fintrack.solution.analytics.p2Html: There are two chart types: a line chart for income and expense dynamics, and a pie chart for category split. Key metrics include totals, comparison with the previous period, and averages. A minimal design and interactive hints make the data easier to read.
fintrack.solution.filters.title: Filters
fintrack.solution.filters.desc: Analytics can be tailored with filters: a specific account and one or more spending categories. The default period is the current month, and users can pick another range.
fintrack.solution.goals.title: Goals & details
fintrack.solution.goals.p1: Another core section is financial goals. It is meant as a tool for deliberate money management: not just putting money aside, but seeing a concrete goal and tracking progress.
fintrack.solution.goals.p2: The main job is to build a savings habit that feels convenient and a little playful. That should lower the stress of planning, help people hit goals, and turn money from abstract numbers into a way to fulfill wishes.
fintrack.solution.createGoal.title: Creating a goal
fintrack.solution.createGoal.p1: Creating a goal is a step-by-step flow: name, target amount, current balance, deadline, and the date saving starts.
fintrack.solution.createGoal.p2Html: This format keeps cognitive load low. Filling in data stays simple, and a progress bar shows which step the user is on.
fintrack.solution.settings.title: Settings & profile
fintrack.solution.settings.desc: Settings cover currency, spending categories, accounts, budget, and visual theme. Sign-in is optional: people can use core features immediately and create an account later to save data. That keeps the app open and accessible.
fintrack.solution.auth.title: Sign-in & registration
fintrack.solution.auth.descHtml:
If someone wants to start tracking right away, they can skip registration. Email sign-in unlocks extra capabilities:
✔ Data saved — nothing is lost when switching devices.
✔ Sync — access from different devices.
✔ Security — an account protects the data.
fintrack.result.title: Outcome
fintrack.result.p1Html: Building Fintrack was a full study of user needs in financial planning. I reviewed existing products, analyzed behavior, and identified the main problems people face. That led to a product that actually simplifies money control and makes budgeting clear.
fintrack.result.p2: The final solution is more than a tracker: it helps people manage money deliberately. Convenience, analytics, and flexibility give control over spending without extra effort.
fintrack.result.p3: I focused on an intuitive interface where every detail serves ease of use. A minimal but informative design makes features easy to find, and considered interaction flows lower cognitive load. Each screen was designed around real needs, so navigation stays logical and accessible.
freshmart.hero.title: Freshmart — healthy food delivery
freshmart.about.title: About the project
freshmart.about.p1Html: Freshmart is a mobile app for ordering and delivering healthy ready meals and groceries. The service offers a wide range of products and dishes, including salads, soups, mains, vegetarian meals, and desserts. Users can also pick up a pre-order at city stores.
freshmart.role.title: My role
freshmart.role.desc: UX/UI designer. Research, concept, visual design, and prototyping.
freshmart.tools.title: Tools
freshmart.tools.desc: Figma, Miro, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator
freshmart.goal.title: ⭐️ Goal
freshmart.goal.desc: Create a convenient mobile app for ordering and delivering healthy ready meals. Choosing and ordering dishes should feel easy.
freshmart.task.title: 📌 Challenge
freshmart.task.desc: Search should be easy and the menu intuitive. Success criteria are simplicity, appeal, and accessibility. The design should support a healthy lifestyle and present dishes in a visually appealing way.
freshmart.audience.title: Target audience
freshmart.audience.intro: People who actively care about their health and want convenient, balanced meals. The age range is wide, from younger adults to older users.
freshmart.audience.1.title: 👱 People who want to lose weight
freshmart.audience.1.desc: Interested in personalized meal plans and low-calorie dishes.
freshmart.audience.2.desc: Busy clients who lack time to cook full meals.
freshmart.audience.3.title: 🏃 Athletes and fitness enthusiasts
freshmart.audience.3.desc: Focused on proper nutrition to support training, performance, and energy levels.
freshmart.audience.4.title: 🧓 People with GI conditions
freshmart.audience.4.desc: People with gastritis and stomach ulcers have to follow strict dietary limits.
freshmart.audience.5.title: 🤱 New mothers
freshmart.audience.5.desc: Need dietary meals to support lactation, plus fast ready food because cooking time is limited.
freshmart.audience.6.title: 🥦 Vegans and vegetarians
freshmart.audience.6.desc: Care about nature, their own well-being, and balanced nutrition.
freshmart.bench.title: Benchmarking
freshmart.bench.p1: The food-delivery market has grown a lot in recent years. People trust delivery more and visit stores less because it is convenient and saves time. Preferences differ by criteria — and one of them is ease of use.
freshmart.bench.p2: In Russia a few apps dominate demand. Among healthy-food delivery services I chose VkusVill, ZhiznMart, Samokat, and Yandex Eats.
freshmart.bench.criteriaIntro: The main points I used for a UX review of the chosen services:
freshmart.bench.c2: 🔍 Search that is easy to find and understand
freshmart.bench.problemsIntro: After analyzing the apps I listed the main problems a user might hit, including:
freshmart.bench.pIssue1: 😤 Search that is hard to use
freshmart.problem.title: Problem framing and hypotheses
freshmart.problem.1.title: 1. Complex UI
freshmart.problem.label: Problem
freshmart.hyp.label: Hypothesis
freshmart.problem.1.problem: Users often spend too long learning an inconvenient, complex UI, which makes core actions hard.
freshmart.problem.1.hyp: If the interface is simple, concise, and clear, people can go from choosing a dish to paying faster — without studying a complex UI.
freshmart.problem.2.title: 2. Choosing a dish
freshmart.problem.2.problem: Users often spend too long choosing food or cannot find the dish they want.
freshmart.problem.2.hyp: If search is convenient and dishes are grouped into categories, people will find items faster and spend less time choosing.
freshmart.problem.3.title: 3. Delivery issues
freshmart.problem.3.problem: Some issues sit outside the app itself — delays, wrong orders, or poor delivery — and they still cause dissatisfaction.
freshmart.problem.3.hyp: If we add real-time courier tracking and push notifications about delivery status, people will stay informed and satisfaction will rise.
freshmart.problem.4.title: 4. Poor support
freshmart.problem.4.problem: This can mean weak in-app support, the delivery issues above, poor food quality, or payment problems — all of which lead to complaints.
freshmart.problem.4.hyp: If we add a convenient support chat, people can resolve issues faster, which should reduce complaints and raise satisfaction.
freshmart.persona.title: User persona
freshmart.persona.name: Anna, 26
freshmart.persona.motivationHtml:
— Tasty, low-calorie food at restaurant quality near home.
— Saving time without sacrificing health.
— Variety in her diet without a complicated search for dishes.
freshmart.persona.goalsHtml:
— Find reasonably priced dishes.
— Build a balanced, low-calorie menu.
— Get the order quickly without delays.
freshmart.persona.painHtml:
— Worries the menu is not diverse enough.
— Hard to find products with a good ingredients list.
freshmart.empathy.title: Empathy map
freshmart.flow.title: User flow
freshmart.solution.title: Solution
freshmart.solution.onboarding.title: Splash screen & onboarding
freshmart.solution.onboarding.desc: The app greets people with bright images of healthy food, sets a positive tone, and immediately shows core features and benefits.
freshmart.solution.auth.title: Sign-in
freshmart.solution.auth.p1: Users can sign in with a phone number — the simplest path. After entering the number they choose where the confirmation code goes: SMS or Telegram.
freshmart.solution.auth.p2: Sign-in can also be skipped so people can explore core features, including the most important part — the menu and dish range. That can save time and keep the focus on choosing food.
freshmart.solution.home.title: Home screen
freshmart.solution.home.desc: On the home screen people can quickly find a dish via search or jump to tracking an active order. They can also see new products and promotions and pick a meal program.
freshmart.solution.menu.title: Menu & product card
freshmart.solution.menu.p1: The menu is easier to scan because dishes are grouped by category. Search stays available in the top bar.
freshmart.solution.menu.p2: The product card is intuitive and the key information is easy to scan. Add-to-cart is available on the cards, so there is no need to open a separate page.
freshmart.solution.search.title: Search & favorites
freshmart.solution.profile.title: Profile & support chat
freshmart.solution.profile.p1: In Profile, users can edit personal data, manage addresses and cards, view order history and favorites, read terms, and sign out.
freshmart.solution.profile.p2: In Chat, users can contact support, leave a review, or file a complaint. Promotions and new-product notifications also arrive here.
freshmart.solution.cart.title: Cart
freshmart.solution.cart.desc: The cart lets people review selected items, adjust quantities, and move easily to checkout.
freshmart.solution.checkout.title: Checkout & order tracking
freshmart.solution.checkout.p1: Checkout is simple and intuitive. Several secure payment options keep the transaction fast and smooth.
freshmart.solution.checkout.p2: Order tracking provides real-time delivery updates so people stay informed at every step.
freshmart.result.title: Outcome
freshmart.result.p1: From idea to final design, this project was about making ordering convenient and intuitive. Step by step I improved the experience — simpler navigation, a structured menu, and a tighter checkout.
freshmart.result.p2: A key task was balancing aesthetics and function while keeping the interface light and easy.
freshmart.result.p3: The result is a visually appealing, understandable product. People value the intuitive design, convenient flows, and the ability to explore the menu without extra steps.
oredesign.hero.title: Online deposit opening redesign
oredesign.context.title: Context
oredesign.context.p1Html: My O!+ Bank is a super-app that combines banking, a mobile-subscriber account, and a marketplace for buying and selling goods in Kyrgyzstan. Opening an online deposit is one of the most requested features. People want to review terms quickly, estimate returns, and open a deposit without friction. I focused the redesign on simplifying the flow and improving the experience.
oredesign.goals.taskIntro: Create a convenient deposit-opening flow that lets the user:
oredesign.goals.task2: ✦ Choose the desired term and amount.
oredesign.goals.task3: ✦ Calculate the final amount with interest.
oredesign.goals.task4: ✦ Open the deposit in a couple of taps.
oredesign.goals.solutionIntro: I reworked the interface to make it intuitive and concise:
oredesign.goals.solution1: ✦ Designed a screen with key deposit information.
oredesign.goals.solution2: ✦ Paid special attention to interactive controls that make parameters easy to set.
oredesign.goals.solution3: ✦ Instant yield calculation so people immediately see how much they will earn.
oredesign.goals.solution4: ✦ As few steps as possible to open a deposit.
oredesign.goals.result1: ✦ Users decide to open a deposit faster.
oredesign.goals.result2: ✦ Less time spent studying terms and doing calculations.
oredesign.goals.result3: ✦ A better experience that supports growth in opened deposits.
oredesign.audience.title: Target audience
oredesign.audience.1.title: 💁‍♀️ Bank clients
oredesign.audience.1.desc: Existing users who want to open a deposit quickly in the app.
oredesign.audience.2.title: 💁 New users
oredesign.audience.2.desc: People considering online deposits as an alternative to visiting a branch.
oredesign.current.title: Current design
oredesign.current.p1: I started by studying the current deposit-opening flow in the app, plus the website, offers, and terms. I tested the feature  and the calculator.
oredesign.current.p2: Opening a deposit in the app is inconvenient today — there is no way to see all offers at once and compare tariffs. People come in and often leave without completing because they are afraid of making a mistake or do not know how to pick the right option.
oredesign.bench.title: Benchmarking
oredesign.bench.p1: Next I ran a competitive analysis and reviewed similar flows  in other banking apps. I noted what might cause friction  during the flow, and what could leave a positive impression  of the interface. I looked at local banks and major Russian apps: Sber, T-Bank, Alfa-Bank, and Ozon Bank.
oredesign.bench.criteriaIntro: The main points I used for the UX review:
oredesign.bench.c4: 💡 Hints and guidance during the flow
oredesign.bench.c6: ⚡️ Number of steps to open a deposit
oredesign.bench.problemsIntro: After analyzing the apps I listed the main problems a user might hit, including:
oredesign.bench.pIssue3: 😤 It is not always obvious how much you will have by the end of the term
oredesign.scenarios.title: Scenarios
oredesign.scenarios.desc: Then I listed the core features and defined what a convenient, understandable online-deposit flow should be. I wrote JTBD and a scenario.
oredesign.solution.title: Solution
oredesign.solution.onboarding.title: Onboarding screen & deposits section
oredesign.solution.onboarding.p1Html: ✦ An info screen now explains key benefits and terms. It lowers anxiety, motivates opening a deposit, and points to the primary action.
oredesign.solution.onboarding.p2: ✦ The deposits section shows all available bank offers. Each card has the essentials for choosing: min. amount, top-up/withdrawal terms, and the rate.
oredesign.solution.open.title: Opening a deposit
oredesign.solution.open.p1: ✦ The screen structure is simpler: focus on key parameters and the final amount, without extra noise.
oredesign.solution.open.p2: ✦ Amount and term are prefilled so people see concrete numbers and can decide faster.
oredesign.solution.open.p3Html: ✦ A carousel of deposit cards makes it easy to switch between terms.
oredesign.solution.open.p4Html: ✦ Users can read the full deposit terms. To save space, terms live on a separate screen.
oredesign.solution.terms.title: Choosing terms
oredesign.solution.terms.p1: ✦ Selecting term and currency shows the matching interest rate. People can judge the benefit quickly without extra steps.
oredesign.solution.amount.title: Entering the amount
oredesign.solution.amount.p1: ✦ Simple, intuitive input, keyboard opens automatically, clean UI.
oredesign.solution.amount.p2: ✦ Convenient amount chips that speed up filling the form.
oredesign.solution.account.title: Choosing the debit account
oredesign.solution.account.p1: ✦ Optimized UI: account selection in a modal.
oredesign.solution.otp.title: OTP & success screen
oredesign.solution.otp.p1Html: ✦ The success screen confirms that the deposit is open. Its job is to signal that the flow is complete and guide the user to the next step.
oredesign.result.title: Outcome
oredesign.result.p1: The redesign made opening an online deposit more transparent and convenient. I reworked the interface so people can understand terms faster, see key parameters at a glance, and decide quickly.
oredesign.result.p2: A key goal was to remove friction. Calculations are clearer and navigation is simpler, which shortened the time to open a deposit.
oredesign.result.p3: Instead of overloaded screens I focused on clear information and understandable steps. Clients now complete deposit opening faster, and a smoother interaction increases engagement and trust.
tbank.hero.title: T-Bank — call center operator interface
tbank.about.title: About the project
tbank.about.p1: Bank call-center operators process hundreds of card-delivery requests every day. They need to check client data quickly, schedule courier meetings, and log the status of each case.
tbank.about.p2: They need a convenient, intuitive interface that shortens processing time, simplifies the job, and helps the bank reduce costs.
tbank.goals.task: Design an internal CRM interface for call-center operators. The tool should simplify scheduling meetings, make request management more transparent, and raise overall team efficiency.
tbank.goals.solution1: ✦ A home page with dashboards, key analytics, stats, and live data for the operator’s current workday.
tbank.goals.solution2: ✦ A table of all requests where operators can see the essentials and open a request card.
tbank.goals.solution3: ✦ Quick actions: call, reschedule a meeting, mark a missed call, and mark a callback.
tbank.goals.solution4: ✦ A logical interface structure so operators can manage requests efficiently.
tbank.goals.result1: ✦ Operators process requests faster. Average time per client went down.
tbank.goals.result2: ✦ Dashboards with live request data help prioritize work.
tbank.goals.result3: ✦ A clear communication structure and timely follow-ups raise client satisfaction.
tbank.story.title: User story
tbank.story.lead: As a call-center operator, I can:
tbank.story.1: ✦ Advise the client on the product they applied for.
tbank.story.2: ✦ Schedule a meeting at a time that works for the client.
tbank.story.3: ✦ Contact the client in chat when needed.
tbank.story.4: ✦ See the client’s work/home address for the meeting, change it, or add a new one.
tbank.story.5: ✦ Use built-in calling tools: start/end a call, hold, mute speaker, mute microphone.
tbank.story.6: ✦ View call history and, if needed, open the client card for extra information.
tbank.hypotheses.title: Hypotheses
tbank.hypotheses.intro: I started with hypotheses. I needed to understand which features would actually help operators work faster. I studied their core tasks and interviewed people who work with calls. I learned which tools they use, which problems they hit, mapped pain points, and formed the main hypotheses from that.
tbank.hypotheses.1.title: Fast access to data
tbank.hypotheses.1.desc: If all needed client data is at hand, the operator can answer immediately instead of searching.
tbank.hypotheses.2.title: Request history
tbank.hypotheses.2.desc: A history of every action on a request lets operators see what is already done and what comes next.
tbank.hypotheses.3.title: Chat
tbank.hypotheses.3.desc: If operators can chat and send messages, contact happens faster.
tbank.hypotheses.4.title: Filters and search
tbank.hypotheses.4.desc: If operators can filter and search requests for their own tasks, they will process them faster.
tbank.hypotheses.5.title: Statistics
tbank.hypotheses.5.desc: If operators can see their call and request stats, they can review their performance and understand how to hit KPI.
tbank.hypotheses.6.title: Quick actions
tbank.hypotheses.6.desc: If operators have buttons for frequent tasks (call, reschedule, missed-call mark), they can process requests faster.
tbank.persona.title: User persona
tbank.persona.intro: I also reviewed call-center employee comments on forums and sites and used them to build a persona and empathy map.
tbank.persona.name: Anastasia, 27
tbank.persona.motivationHtml:
— Hit the monthly KPI percentage for a bonus.
— Raise client loyalty and collect positive feedback.
tbank.persona.goalsHtml:
— Advise bank clients, recommend fitting products, and schedule meetings.
— Process as many requests as possible.
— Hit the shift target for processed requests.
tbank.persona.painHtml:
— Too much time is spent processing and entering data after a call.
— Clients often do not answer.
— A confusing interface with too many unused tabs.
tbank.empathy.title: Empathy map
tbank.empathy.doesHtml:
— Processes client requests.
— Advises clients on bank products.
— Schedules courier meetings.
tbank.empathy.hearsHtml:
— “I can’t talk right now.”
— “My plans changed.”
— “I want the card as soon as possible.”
— “Tell me about the benefits of this card.”
tbank.empathy.thinksHtml:
— “I need to process this request fast — I don’t have time to search.”
— “I’m afraid of making a mistake, especially when the client is in a hurry.”
— “It would be easier if all the needed data were at hand.”
tbank.empathy.seesHtml:
— A complex interface with many tabs.
— Clients often change their plans.
— Other operators also struggle and come over with questions.
— The bank’s client base is growing.
tbank.solution.title: Solution
tbank.solution.home.title: Home screen
tbank.solution.home.p1: At first I imagined a simple form for scheduling meetings, then realized operators need a more considered system. They handle a high volume of requests each day, so the interface should help them navigate data — not just display it.
tbank.solution.home.p2: I started with the home page. I wanted it useful and informative without overload. A request list came first, but it did not explain the workday. I then added dashboards — how many requests arrived, how many are done, how many are still in queue. That immediately made the process more transparent.
tbank.solution.requests.title: Requests screen
tbank.solution.requests.descHtml:
This screen should help operators find the right requests quickly and work them efficiently. I structured the list so status, client data, and meeting time are visible at a glance.
I also added filters and search, plus a one-tap jump to the client card to clarify details or get in touch.
tbank.solution.process.title: Request handling screen
tbank.solution.process.p1: Tapping a client in the list opens the request details. Operators can see core data, contact the client, confirm delivery details, and send the request into the workflow. The interface supports fast client interaction and convenient delivery setup.
tbank.solution.process.p2: On one screen the operator can contact the client and fill or edit all needed data — tools stay at hand, which speeds up the work.
tbank.solution.status.title: Changing request status
tbank.solution.status.descHtml: Operators manage request status by stage. When they start work they set “In progress”. After the request is processed and handed to a courier, status automatically becomes “Completed”. During the call they can also set “Cancelled” or “Callback needed” if more details are required.
tbank.solution.call.title: Call panel
tbank.solution.call.desc: One click starts a call. The number loads automatically, and the control panel appears: mute, hold, or hang up. All functions sit in one place for speed.
tbank.solution.hints.title: Product hint tooltips
tbank.solution.hints.desc: Hovering the icon next to a product name shows a tooltip with benefits. Operators can orient in details quickly and answer client questions on the spot.
tbank.solution.chat.title: Client chat
tbank.solution.chat.p1Html: Tapping “Open chat” opens a dialogue with the client. The operator can send a message and confirm delivery details. The client can also reach out to change or clarify information.
tbank.solution.chat.p2Html: From the chat window the operator can jump to other messages. The shared messenger covers client threads, corporate messages, and chats with colleagues.
tbank.solution.confirm.title: Request confirmation
tbank.solution.confirm.descHtml: After the call and filling in the data, the request is ready for the courier. A modal lets the operator check the information before sending. They can cancel and edit if needed.
tbank.solution.success.title: Meeting scheduled successfully
tbank.solution.success.descHtml: The request is processed and assigned to an available courier. The operator’s work is done, and status is set automatically to “Completed”. A modal confirms success, and “Continue” returns them to the requests table without extra steps.
tbank.result.title: Outcome
tbank.result.p1: I accounted for the negative user experience, covered core needs, and optimized the operator workspace. An intuitive interface simplifies the job and lets operators process requests faster. That improves day-to-day work and should increase issued products — which helps the bank’s revenue.
